findingDetails.title: Child-dispatch Gate 3 exception is missing from the skill and implementation command
findingDetails.evidence: AGENTS.md pre-resolves Gate 3 for non-interactive child dispatches. The skill says to ask and wait for A/B/C/D on file changes and forbids proceeding without confirmation; speckit-implement.yaml also says stop, ask, and wait. A child that follows these lower-level instructions literally can wait for an unavailable answer.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The unconditional wait appears in the canonical skill and implementation command; the root exception is the conflicting consumer policy.
findingDetails.recommendation: State the child-dispatch exemption next to the skill and command Gate 3 waits while retaining the question for interactive sessions.
findingDetails.claim: The skill and implementation command omit the root policy exception for child dispatches and can block an already-bound non-interactive worker.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the root exception, both skill copies, and the command Gate 3 wording; searched those surfaces for the child-dispatch environment markers. The root exception is explicit, but the skill and command text does not repeat it.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The root policy has higher precedence, and a dispatch prompt may carry the exemption explicitly, which can prevent a compliant worker from waiting.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A runtime conformance check proves child-dispatch markers suppress both prompts, and the skill and command document that behavior.

findingDetails.title: Repository-era catalog overstates the no-specs case
findingDetails.evidence: The catalog says that no specs folder means v3. The implementation sets v3 only when a distinct .opencode/specs root or description residue exists, and otherwise returns unknown when neither layout root exists.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Directly compared the catalog sentence with the layout predicate and returned kind in repo-era.mjs.
findingDetails.recommendation: Say that an existing legacy .opencode/specs root with no specs root is v3; a checkout with neither root is unknown.
findingDetails.claim: The catalog omits the legacy-root condition, so its sentence also describes a checkout with neither root as v3.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The catalog introduces both roots and its v3 example could be read as assuming the legacy root exists; the implementation and tests confirm v3 for that legacy-root case.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The sentence may intend the ordinary v3-only layout, but it does not state that the legacy root must exist.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: The catalog is explicitly scoped to repositories where the legacy root exists, or another code path forces v3 when neither root exists.
